title: The Ironies Of The Big Smoke

contact_edits.before: Xuan Fraser gives a beautifully controlled performance as Thomas, urbane witheruptions, and Brian Marler a winning one as Simon, appealing with complications. Philip Akins production is handicapped by a playground set that serves little practical or metaphorical purpose, but it brings out all the scripts excitements. It starts like the urban play we've all been waiting for. It can't sustain that, but it ends on an oddly hopeful note that's both touching and persuasive. The character who's been keenest to leave town is resigned, maybe even reconciled, to staying. The city may not be Toronto the good, but it isn't all bad either. - Toronto the Good runs until March 1. Call 416-504-9971 for information.
